Subject: RE: CODEX: question about normalization2

No problem! Since your data is also WES, you can directly use the attached segmentation script. Note that you need to specify the order of your samples. For example, if you samples come in an order of normal1, tumor1, normal2, tumor2, normal3, tumor3, …, then you need to use the command below:

N0 = dim(Y_qc)[1]
nsamp = length(sampname_qc)/2
relCN = matrix(0,N0,nsamp)

tumorid = 2*(1:nsamp) % the indices of tumor samples normalid = tumorid -1 % the indices of normal samples

Also you need to install the package attached as well (don’t install directly from the CRAN, it’s not updated).

Let me know if you've additional questions!

Yuchao

Hi Tim,

Yes, Brad is correct -- the multi-sample normalization model by CODEX doesn't require paired case-control data. I have a script for segmentation that I use for the paired case-control setting. However that's for WES not targeted sequencing. Our previous experience showed that the default segmentation by CODEX and the newer version (that compared tumor versus normal) didn't make much difference if any at all. Why don’t you give it a try first and see if you can get something out of it. Let me know if you need additional help -- I can send you something later this week once I've modified the segmentation script for targeted sequencing.

Cheers,
Yuchao

Hello,

It is the latter. It just needs to know the indecies of the normal samples. Also K can not be greater than the number of normals. So if you have less than 15 normals you will need to adjust the range.

Also if you have a simple name scheme you could do something savvy like normal_index=grep('Normal',sampname)

-Brad

Dear Yuchao Jiang

I am working for IPCT in MD Anderson Cancer Center.

I have gotten the modified version of CODEX for targeted sequencing and am testing CODEX with our data ( tumor & normal samples).

I have one question regarding the function, normalizatio2.

The following is a part of the codex_targeted.r:

normObj=normalize2(Y_qc,gc_qc,K=1:15,normal_index=29:44)



I believe normal_index=29:44 indicates the index of normal sample in sampname.

My question is that do I need to pair tumor samples with normal samples.

For example, sampname=c(t1,t2,t3,n1,n2,n3), where t and n denote tumor and normal, respectively. Then should t1 and n1 be paired? t2 and n2 paired? t3 and n3 paired? Or it does not matter as long as normal_index indicates the index of normal samples?



Thank you
